claim: Neural sequence models generalise well on random splits but collapse on systematic recombination of known parts (new primitive in composed commands, max compound divergence, new roles in COGS). Random 99.8% vs add-jump 1.2% best; CFQ 97-98% vs 15-19%; COGS in-distribution 96-99% vs 16-35%.
agent_test: Background; test own agent on a held-out recombination set of its own operators vs random split at equal tokens

claim: Much of the early Transformer failure was setup, not architecture: embedding scaling, early stopping on IID data and relative positions lifted PCFG productivity 50 to 85%, COGS 35 to 81%, SCAN length to 100%. IID validation hides the gap.
agent_test: Never select prompts or settings on in-distribution items; report on a compound-shifted split

claim: Length extrapolation (productivity) is harder than lexical systematicity: SCAN length best 13.8-20.8%; PCFG productivity Transformer 0.50 and LSTM 0.30; part of the failure is the model not learning when to stop (EOS).
agent_test: Test the agent on tasks 2x longer than any seen in its prompt exemplars

claim: Explicit decomposition into ordered subproblems (least-to-most) closes the SCAN length gap in prompted code-davinci-002: 99.7% vs 16.2% chain of thought and 16.7% standard, from 14 exemplars; residual errors are nested-scope errors (13 of the test set).
agent_test: Compare decompose-then-solve against plain CoT at equal tokens on compositional splits; note one paper only, code-davinci-002 is a model that is no longer served

claim: Meta-learning over many fresh compositional episodes yields human-level systematicity in a small Transformer: 82.4% vs human 80.7%, with human-like errors, near zero error on SCAN lexical splits; fails on structural splits (length, COGS structural).
agent_test: Low relevance (needs training); skip unless fine-tuning is allowed
note: Gap search: abstract only re-read; no replication on structural splits and no prompt-only version found (gap 8 open).

claim: LLMs answer both sub-facts yet fail the composed 2-hop question; the gap is about 40% across GPT-3 sizes, 42.9% ChatGPT, 23.0% GPT-4; self-ask lifts 45.7% to 79.6% (InstructGPT Davinci-002, Compositional Celebrities).
agent_test: Measure a gap = P(both parts right) minus P(composed right) with and without an explicit sub-question step

claim: Correct final answers in LLM multi-step tasks often hide wrong steps: 82.3% of correct 4x2-digit multiplications had a wrong intermediate step; 3x3 multiplication ChatGPT 55%, GPT-4 59%; accuracy falls with depth. Consistent with pattern matching on linearised subgraphs.
agent_test: Audit intermediate steps for a sample of correct answers; track step-level error rate

claim: Accuracy tracks output or input probability, not just logic: GPT-4 shift cipher 51% for high-probability output vs 13% for low; counterfactual rule variants lower accuracy (GPT-3.5 parseable programs 99% to 62-75%).
agent_test: Run each task in a counterfactual-rule variant; a gap means pattern reuse

claim: Learned knowledge is directional: GPT-4 knows celebrity parent 79% of time but the reverse 33%; fine-tuned GPT-3 96.7% forward, about 0 reversed (50.0% in the NameToDescription matched order). Fails a symmetry that a structured store would satisfy. Does not occur when fact is in context.
agent_test: Store each fact with its inverse in memory and test retrieval from either direction

claim: Writing reasoning as executable code with an interpreter removes arithmetic failure: GSM-HARD CoT 65.6 to 20.1% vs PAL 61.5% (drop 14.3 points); object counting 96.7%.
agent_test: Compare CoT with code-as-thought at equal tokens on large-number variants

claim: LLMs bind entities and attributes with internal binding-ID vectors, a variable-binding-like code; mean interventions drop accuracy from above 99% to below 3% (Pythia and LLaMA).
agent_test: Background; no agent test

claim: Grokked Transformers compose two-hop facts in-distribution only after about 50x more steps than needed to fit train data and still show zero OOD composition after 2M steps; weakly supports that composition is learned slowly, not built in.
agent_test: Background

claim: Program-induction systems (DreamCoder: 3.7% to 79.6% on SyGuS; Bayesian LLM hypothesis proposers, R2 .81 vs humans; probabilistic LoT with LLM translation) are working language-of-thought builds. Benchmark evidence is thin outside DreamCoder.
agent_test: Try propose-many then score hypotheses vs single answer at equal tokens

claim: LLMs show human-like content effects and do well on abstract relational tasks (GPT-3 beats undergraduates on digit matrices, OR 1.88 to 6.27) but are weak on abstract reasoning out of distribution; evidence mixed on whether variable-like abstraction exists.
agent_test: Test with abstract-symbol versions of the same problem; compare with content version

claim: Whether LoT is the best explanation of cognition is disputed: classical argument is abductive, connectionist replies (tensor products, Smolensky) are answered by Fodor-McLaughlin; empirical LoT cluster is claimed by Quilty-Dunn et al. These lines were not opened.
agent_test: None; philosophical background

claim: Latent continuous thought can beat words on search-heavy logic (Coconut ProsQA 97.0% vs CoT 77.5%) but loses on GSM8k (34.1% vs 42.9%); a words-only thought medium is not always best.
agent_test: Out of reach for a prompt-only scaffold; background
note: Gap search: GSM8k CoT 42.9 vs Coconut 34.1; ProsQA 77.5 vs 97.0; no independent replication found (gap 9 open).

claim: Reasoning-trained models shrink but do not remove sensitivity to output probability, rare task variants and surface perturbations: o1-preview shift cipher 47% (low-probability outputs) to 92% (high); same accuracy on rare and common acronyms (99.9 vs 100%) but many more thinking tokens on the rare one; GSM-NoOp irrelevant clause still cuts o1-preview accuracy.
agent_test: Pair every test item with a rare or counterfactual twin and an irrelevant-clause twin; report the gap; use thinking-token spend as a difficulty signal

claim: Productivity (longer compositions) still fails in current reasoning models: on Tower of Hanoi, Checker Jumping, River Crossing and Blocks World, o3-mini, DeepSeek-R1 and Claude 3.7 Sonnet thinking collapse to near zero beyond a model-specific depth, reduce thinking tokens near the collapse, and do not improve when the algorithm is given in the prompt. At low complexity non-thinking models win at equal compute.
schema_part: O (delegate exact execution to code or tools)
agent_test: Compare in-prompt execution with code execution on 8-12 step procedures; check whether collapse moves

claim: Infant abstract rule learning (Marcus 1999, ABB patterns) exists but is small and conditional: meta-analysis of 20 reports, 63 experiments, 1,318 infants gives Hedges g 0.25 (95% CI 0.09 to 0.40); stronger with meaningful stimuli; likely publication bias; Marcus 2007 found no learning from tones unless primed with speech. Rats also transfer XYX rules (Murphy 2008, abstract only).
agent_test: Background; do not treat human rule learning as evidence for a rigid symbolic code

claim: Hidden-step errors grow with difficulty: among solutions with correct final answers, 3.5% (GSM8K), 18.8% (MATH), 32.2% (OlympiadBench) and 51.8% (Omni-MATH) contain a wrong step; prompted critics (o1-mini F1 87.9, QwQ-32B 71.5, GPT-4o 61.9) beat small process reward models on hard sets.
agent_test: Run a strongest-model step critic on a sample of correct-answer traces and count flagged steps

claim: In training-from-scratch transformers the reversal curse is a binding-like failure (0.0% reversal accuracy under standard next-token training); a JEPA design or memory layers removes it. It is an architecture fix, with no frontier-model test found.
agent_test: Store each fact in both directions in agent memory and test reverse recall

claim: Open LLMs contain head circuits that act like variable binding: symbol abstraction heads, symbolic induction heads and retrieval heads; ablating them drives the correct-answer probability to zero; Llama-3.1 70B 95% on 2-shot rule induction.
agent_test: Background only
